chapter: La Cigalle and settling in Paris
title: The music played at La Cigalle
summary: The Cigalle was a listening room for acts. Butler's band played swing, bebop, waltzes, guarachas and mambos jazzed up, in contrast to Archey's Dixieland and Coleman's swing bands.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Was it an all-jazz gig or were you playing for acts at La Cigalle too?
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Oh yes, it was playing for public, no dancing at all, just attractions.
And what kind of music - the Archey band was a Dixieland band -
[ ], same as your place.
Uh huh.
But Archey was a Dixieland band.
Archey was a Dixieland band, Coleman is a swing band or Dixie band?
Big - well, they called it the New New Orleans [ ], he called it -
Uh hh -
At Jimmy Ryan's. [ ] -
Now you're talking about Archey.
Yeah, Archey, yeah.
Yeah, that's Dixieland, we already did that one. Bill Coleman's band, swing band or was it D-
Swing band -
Swing band. And the Jacques Butler band, swing band or -
Yeah.
Strictly swing.

We played all kinds of things. We played very tough numbers - we played bebop, we played everything. We played Viennese waltzes, we played the guarachas, we played mambos, we played all kinds of things, you know.
So it was a strictly music place, but it wasn't strictly jazz 'cause youuwere playing some non-jazz material. Or were you jazzing these mambos -

Jazzin' 'em, yeah. (Sings some Latin music), jazz - things like that, you know (laughs). I forget the name of that but it was very popular in Europe (sings), they call it guaracho [guaracha?], fast, you know.
Uh huh.
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Yeah, it was jazz. We played everything, we'd play all kinds of - real modern, real old. We had an arrangement on "Jada" that we made from memory, we had.
